- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Here are the findings, verified against the actual file:

---

## Performance Review Findings

### 1. `ALL_SPORTS` recalculated every render (line 292) — HIGH IMPACT

`Object.keys(SPORT_LABELS)` is called on every render even though `SPORT_LABELS` is a module-level constant. The result is identical on every call. Move it to module scope:

```ts
// module scope
const ALL_SPORTS = Object.keys(SPORT_LABELS);
```

The secondary issue is that `ALL_SPORTS` is used as the `useState` initializer at line 293, so it runs the key extraction on mount, and then again on every subsequent render (at line 292) just to compute `allActive` at line 302. The module-scope fix eliminates both redundant calls.

---

### 2. `TIME_PALETTES` array literal reconstructed every render (lines 334-340)

The array is declared inline inside the component. Since it never changes, it should live at module scope. As-is, a new array with 5 object literals is allocated on every render.

---

### 3. `contrastText()` redeclared every render (lines 351-354) — LOW/MEDIUM

The function is declared with `function` syntax inside the component body, producing a new function object each render. More importantly, `contrastText` is called immediately on line 355 with `accentColor`, which itself can only change when `searchSport` or `currentHour` changes. Move the function to module scope; optionally memoize `accentFg` with `useMemo` keyed on `accentColor`.

---

### 4. City derivations — six passes over `courts` array every render (lines 422-434) — MEDIUM IMPACT

Six derived values are computed unconditionally from `courts` on every render:
- `uniqueCities` (spread + Set + sort)
- `cityCounts` (reduce)
- `popularCities` (sort + slice on a copy)
- `otherCities` (filter with `includes` — O(n²) against `popularCities`)
- `filteredPopular` (filter)
- `filteredOther` (filter)

`uniqueCities`, `cityCounts`, `popularCities`, and `otherCities` depend only on `courts`. They should all be wrapped in a single `useMemo([courts])`. `filteredPopular` and `filteredOther` depend additionally on `cityInput` and can be a second `useMemo([popularCities, otherCities, cityFilter])`. Note that `otherCities.filter(c => !popularCities.includes(c))` at line 431 is O(n²) — a `Set` lookup would be O(n).

---

### 5. `filteredCourts` — inline filter every render (lines 416-420)

Filtered on every render regardless of whether `searchName` or `courts` changed. Should be wrapped in `useMemo([searchName, courts])`. The `searchName.trim()` is called twice (line 416 and 418) where a single variable would suffice.

---

### 6. Stats bar `.sort()` on every render (lines 857-860)

The array literal built at lines 851-856 depends only on `stats` (a TanStack Query result). The `.sort()` runs on every render even when `stats` hasn't changed, including re-renders triggered by `hoveredStat` state changes (which happen on every mouse-enter/leave event over the stats bar). Wrap in `useMemo([stats])`.

---

### 7. `PopularCourtCard` — `hovered`/`btnHovered` state (lines 189-190, 197-275) — MEDIUM IMPACT

Two `useState` variables drive purely visual effects. The card already has `group` on line 197, and the image scale at line 207 already uses `group-hover:scale-105` (pure CSS). The remaining JS-driven hover effects are:
- `borderColor` on the `Card` (line 198): could be done with CSS custom properties or `group-hover:border-[color]` with Tailwind arbitrary values
- `SportPill variant` switching (line 231): cannot be done in pure CSS without JS, but could be unified into `hovered` state instead of a second bool
- `CardTitle color` (line 248): same as border, CSS `group-hover` can handle it
- `boxShadow` on the button (line 275): this is what `btnHovered` exclusively drives; CSS `group-hover` or `:hover` on the `<Button>` itself can handle it

Eliminating both state variables removes 2 event handlers × N cards from the event delegation tree and prevents N card re-renders on every hover event. The `btnHovered` state is straightforwardly replaceable with a CSS `:hover` rule or Tailwind `hover:shadow-[...]`.

---

### 8. Hero image preload guard (lines 393-402) — CORRECT, minor note

The guard `if (prev.has(nextIdx)) return prev;` at line 397 is correct: returning the same `prev` reference tells React the state did not change, so no re-render is triggered. The logic is sound. The only minor observation is that `loadedHeroImages` grows monotonically (never shrinks) — for 5 hero images this is harmless.

---

### 9. `handleSearch` and `toggleSport` — new function objects every render (lines 295-301, 357-365)

Neither is wrapped in `useCallback`. `toggleSport` is passed as an event handler to each sport-filter button (likely N sport chips). `handleSearch` is passed to the search button. Wrapping both in `useCallback` prevents N child prop-change events on unrelated re-renders. `toggleSport` has no external deps (uses functional updater); `handleSearch` depends on `searchName`, `searchSport`, `searchCity`, `searchDate`, `searchTime`, `setLocation`.

---

### Summary table

| # | Location | Issue | Recommended fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | line 292 | `Object.keys(SPORT_LABELS)` every render | Move to module scope |
| 2 | lines 334-340 | `TIME_PALETTES` array literal every render | Move to module scope |
| 3 | lines 351-354 | `contrastText` function redeclared every render | Move to module scope |
| 4 | lines 422-434 | 6 passes over `courts` every render | `useMemo([courts])` + `useMemo([..., cityFilter])` |
| 5 | lines 416-420 | `filteredCourts` filter every render | `useMemo([searchName, courts])` |
| 6 | lines 857-860 | `.sort()` on stats array every render incl. hover re-renders | `useMemo([stats])` |
| 7 | lines 189-190 | `hovered`/`btnHovered` state on every card | Replace with CSS `group-hover` / `:hover` |
| 8 | lines 393-402 | Hero preload guard | Correct — no change needed |
| 9 | lines 295-301, 357-365 | `toggleSport`, `handleSearch` recreated every render | `useCallback` |
